message.content:
A CPU (Central Processing Unit) and a GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) are both processors but they’re designed for different workloads:

| Feature | CPU | GPU |
|---------|-----|-----|
| **Primary purpose** | General‑purpose computing – handles everything from OS tasks to application logic. | Parallel graphics rendering – originally for rasterizing images, now also used for data‑parallel compute tasks. |
| **Core count & design** | Few cores (2–32 in consumer CPUs), each core is powerful, with deep pipelines, branch prediction, large caches, and complex control logic. | Hundreds or thousands of simpler cores optimized for throughput; each core does less work individually but many can run simultaneously. |
| **Execution style** | Serial/low‑latency: one instruction per cycle on a few threads, heavy emphasis on single‑thread performance. | Massively parallel: thousands of lightweight threads executing the same instruction stream (SIMD). |
| **Memory hierarchy** | Large L1/L2/L3 caches per core, sophisticated cache coherence protocols, high memory bandwidth per core. | Smaller per‑core caches, relies on high‑bandwidth shared memory (VRAM) and efficient memory coalescing. |
| **Typical workloads** | Control flow heavy tasks, branching, I/O, operating system services, database queries, web servers. | Data‑parallel tasks: image/video processing, scientific simulations, machine learning inference/training, cryptocurrency mining. |
| **Programming model** | Traditional imperative programming, multi‑threading via OS threads or libraries like OpenMP. | SIMD/SIMT models (CUDA, OpenCL, Vulkan compute shaders); requires explicit parallelization. |
| **Energy efficiency** | Optimized for low latency per operation; higher power draw per core when fully utilized. | Optimized for throughput per watt; very energy‑efficient at scale for suitable workloads. |

In short, a CPU excels at handling diverse, irregular tasks with low latency, while a GPU shines when you have a huge amount of similar operations that can be performed in parallel. That’s why modern systems often combine both: the CPU orchestrates overall execution, and the GPU accelerates the parts that benefit from massive parallelism.
